findings.recommendation: An SMTP send is not idempotent: when the relay accepts the message but its answer arrives after SEND_TIMEOUT, the mailer gives up and, if it reports that as `Unavailable`, the job is released and the recipient gets the e-mail twice (up to twelve times while the relay stays slow — the very situation this change is for). Give each job a stable Message-ID derived from `job.id` so retries are recognisable downstream, or have the mailer distinguish a timeout after DATA from a refused connection and not retry it blindly. Confidence is low: the mailer implementation, which decides how a timeout is reported, is not part of the diff.
findings.title: A send that times out after the relay accepted it is sent again

findings.recommendation: The worker exports only outcome counters (`notifier_jobs_total{outcome}`) and a liveness beat. When it falls behind — a slow relay taking close to SEND_TIMEOUT per message, or more e-mails queued than one worker sends — `/healthz` stays green and the counters keep rising, so an operator sees nothing until users report late e-mails. Record the send duration (a histogram) and expose the queue depth or the age of the oldest pending job. Confidence is low: such a gauge may already be exported outside the diff.
findings.title: No metric shows the backlog or the send latency
